title: Labels Charged per Return Parcel Set
content:
Shoeboxes travel in their own carton, and large returns without footwear need more than one label. The Returns & Exchanges return shipping fee is the label fee times the number of labels, and the number of labels follows what travelled, as the return's inspection entries show it.

## Number of labels

| What the inspection entries show | Labels charged |
|---|---|
| Footwear in a shoebox together with other units | 2 — one per parcel, two parcels, because shoeboxes travel in their own carton |
| More than four units and no footwear | One for every four units begun |
| Any other return | 1 |

- **Footwear in a shoebox:** inspection entries carrying a box condition (original box intact, original box damaged or used as shipper, or no original box). **Other units:** inspection entries whose box condition is not applicable.
- **Units:** the units on all of the return's inspection entries, whatever their grade or outcome.

## Counting units with no footwear

| Units | Labels |
|---|---|
| 4 | 1 |
| 5 | 2 |
| 8 | 2 |
| 9 | 3 |

Examples (hypothetical): a return of trainers and two shirts takes 2 labels; a return of six pairs of shoes and nothing else takes 1 label, since footwear travelled; a return of seven tops takes 2 labels.
